description: REQ-21 never states the invocation topology of note-publish-live.py: is it (a) wired into run.sh's Mode-B branch and thus reachable by the unattended daily wake once AUTONOMY=on, or (b) a standalone script only ever invoked manually/out-of-band with an explicit CLI draft-key argument, never called by run.sh at all? The requirement's own name ('Real Mode-B publish path') and its placement conceptually under REQ-7 ('mode = B ... the skill SHALL publish directly') strongly imply (a) — an automated per-wake trigger. But the Sprint 2.5 plan text describes something that only matches (b): a one-off manual action on ONE specific, already-known, already-verified draft key ('nfb2ace9f0ed8'), 'verified by the main agent' (a human-supervised action, not an unattended runtime step). REQ-21 also never states the boolean composition between AUTONOMY (mode A/B) and NOTE_LIVE_PUBLISH: does the real-publish path require AUTONOMY=on AND NOTE_LIVE_PUBLISH=1 together, or can NOTE_LIVE_PUBLISH=1 alone (with no mode/AUTONOMY check inside note-publish-live.py at all) trigger a real click regardless of mode? As written, a future implementer could wire note-publish-live.py into run.sh with ONLY a NOTE_LIVE_PUBLISH check and no explicit AUTONOMY==B gate, meaning a stray/leftover NOTE_LIVE_PUBLISH=1 in the install's shared .env (e.g. left over from a Sprint-2.5 manual test) would cause the NEXT automated daily wake — run under whatever mode happens to be configured, potentially still nominally 'Mode A' if run.sh's Mode-A branch is bypassed by a bug, or definitely once AUTONOMY flips to on per REQ-20's stated roadmap — to real-publish a brand-new, same-day-generated article completely unattended, with none of the Sprint 2.5 human/main-agent verification step this same sprint plan describes as the actual safety mechanism for the ONLY currently-approved real-publish use case. The task's own review question #4 asks exactly this: 'Is there any ambiguity that could let a future implementation accidentally publish from the daily unattended ... wake?' — Yes: the spec is silent on whether note-publish-live.py is wired into the daily loop's control flow at all, and silent on the required AND-composition of its two gating conditions.

evidence.snippet: REQ-21 Real Mode-B publish path. The skill SHALL provide a REAL publish path (`lib/note-publish-live.py` or equivalent) that, given a note draft key already carrying a validated 記事タイプ=有料/¥500 configuration and a cover + visuals, drives the browser to click 投稿する/更新する for real... The real-publish path SHALL require an explicit, separate trigger (env var or CLI flag, e.g. NOTE_LIVE_PUBLISH=1) so it can never fire from the default Mode-A wake.
